But seriously, I'm fond of the .260 Rem and 7mm-08, which are standardized versions of 6.5 and 7mm wildcats of the .308. In fact, I'm all about .308 variants. Very nice case, that. The .375 H&H is neat too, being the smallest legal dangerous game cartrige, and very versitile in its own right.

I carry 9mm, though, and keep 5.56 in my home defense weapon.

I should add that what's nice about the .308 case is its inherent efficiency. Because it takes less powder for a given bullet velocity, the powder burns more completely earlier, so the .308 itself only gains/loses around 20 ft/s per inch of barrel, compare that to the 75ft/s or so lost per inch with the 5.56. This seems to carry over to the wildcat rounds. For example, with the .338 Federal you get the ballistics of the 7mm Rem Mag with the same weight bullets, but with about 20% less recoil. And the .260 Rem is easily the equal of the vaunted, super-efficient 6.5 Creedmoor or 6.5x47 Lapua, but less expensive and more readily available.

.22 lr, .44 mag, 30-06, .45 ACP, 12 GA, .22-250. That's about all I have.

My all-time favorite, though, is the .22 lr.

In handguns, I like the 45s. Powerful, but without the high pressure blast, just a nice solid thump.

I also like the .32 acp. Sort of like a .22 all grown up, and always chambered in interesting little guns.

In rifles, my favorite is the 6.5mm Swede. Plenty of accuracy and all the power you need, but not too much. I like rifles that are slender and graceful, and they are best with medium-powered rounds.

Colabri used to make a powderless .22 that would produce airgun ballistics out of a rifle or pistol. They don't make them any more, replacing them with a stronger round because sometimes they would hang up in tighter rifle bores. It's a shame because it allowed you to do things with your .22s that you'd never otherwise do, like shooting at leaves on the surface of a pond or knocking pine cones out to the branches of a tree. You could also forgo the ear protection, too.

I also like reduced-power 12 gauge slugs. Like the 45 pistols, plenty of thump with less blast.

For defensive use I still like the .40 S&W. Everybody seems to be migrating back to the 9mm because you get faster repeat shots. I like the .40 because it performs well in short-barreled, concealable pistols, producing more power than even a .357 mag (if your barrel is under 3 inches). There's always a tradeoff between power and controllability - some people draw the line between the 9mm and the .380, I draw it between the .40 and the 9mm.
